Progress Note: Roger's First Session

Date: [Insert Date]

Session Date: [Insert Date]

Client: Roger

Presenting Issues: Roger is experiencing anxiety and depression, with scores of 2 and 3 on the anxiety and depression scales, respectively. He reports difficulty focusing, which is distressing for him. Roger has been living at the Turning Point shelter and is currently collecting disability for a Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI).

History: Roger has a history of substance use, but reports no current desire to use due to the negative consequences it has caused in his life. He is motivated to address his current struggles and improve his overall well-being.

Intervention: During the session, Roger and I discussed his current challenges and goals. I introduced the concept of cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT) and its application in addressing anxiety and depression. We also explored strategies for improving focus and concentration.

Response: Roger reported feeling overwhelmed and struggling to cope with his emotions. He expressed a desire to learn new skills and strategies to manage his anxiety and depression. Roger was receptive to the idea of CBT and expressed a willingness to work on his focus and concentration.

Assessment: Roger's anxiety and depression scores indicate a moderate level of distress. However, his motivation to address these issues and his willingness to work on his focus and concentration suggest a positive starting point for treatment.

Next Steps: Roger will continue to work on his focus and concentration skills through a combination of cognitive restructuring, mindfulness, and relaxation techniques. We will also explore strategies for managing anxiety and depression, including exposure and response prevention. Roger will be encouraged to practice these skills regularly and report back to me on his progress.

Rating: Roger's anxiety and depression scores are currently at 2 and 3, respectively. His focus and concentration skills are a concern, but he is motivated to work on improving these areas. With consistent effort and practice, Roger has the potential to make significant progress in addressing his anxiety and depression.

Recommendations: Roger should continue to practice his focus and concentration skills regularly, aiming to increase his productivity and overall quality of life. He should also explore ways to manage his anxiety and depression, including seeking support from friends and family, engaging in regular exercise, and practicing relaxation techniques.

Follow-up: Roger will be seen again in [insert number] weeks to assess his progress and adjust his treatment plan as needed.
